topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning objectives and framing how genetic mutations drive the functional hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and growth factor signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt signaling cascades confer self-sufficiency in growth signals and insensitivity to growth inhibition.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells arrest at immature, proliferative stages across hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal epithelial carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 signaling
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells resist programmed cell death through the inactivation of p53 and the dysregulation of pro- and anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and growth control hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine telomere maintenance, senescence bypass, and p53-mediated stress responses, concluding the survey of cell-intrinsic growth control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biochemical mechanisms, tissue specificity, and oncogenic consequences of altered cellular metabolism and the Warburg effect.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the requirement for new blood vessel formation to supply growing tumors with oxygen and nutrients through the angiogenic switch.

topics.label: Mechanisms and dynamics of cancer invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step metastatic cascade, diagnostic tracking via liquid biopsies, metastatic inefficiency, and the genomic characteristics of secondary tumors.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarizing how cancer hallmarks converge and providing final closing remarks.
